replacements.proposed_text: Plate-forme en saillie sur la façade d’un bâtiment, bordée d’une balustrade et accessible depuis l’intérieur.
replacements.accepted_text: Plate-forme en saillie sur la façade d’un bâtiment, entourée d’une balustrade.
replacements.reason: Concrete projecting building platform with a balustrade. Accepted wording keeps the common core also attested in the original 1935 definition; interior-access wording is omitted from the accepted adaptation.

replacements.proposed_text: Titre porté par les chevaliers et les baronnets en Grande-Bretagne.
replacements.accepted_text: Titre porté par les chevaliers et les baronnets en Grande-Bretagne, placé devant leur prénom.
replacements.reason: French masculine invariant borrowing for the title of knights/baronets, before a given name. Fixed Sir supplies the title and /sœʁ/; retained CNRTL independently labels lowercase sir nom masculin and shows lower/uppercase title use. Ordinary English polite address is excluded.

replacements.proposed_text: Sir, the title borne by knights and baronets in Great Britain.
replacements.accepted_text: Sir: the British title used before a knight’s or baronet’s given name; not the general polite English form of address.
replacements.reason: French masculine invariant borrowing for the title of knights/baronets, before a given name. Fixed Sir supplies the title and /sœʁ/; retained CNRTL independently labels lowercase sir nom masculin and shows lower/uppercase title use. Ordinary English polite address is excluded.

replacements.proposed_text: Sir，英国授予爵士及从男爵的称号。
replacements.accepted_text: Sir：英国骑士和从男爵所用的称号，置于其名字前；此处不指普通敬称“先生”。
replacements.reason: French masculine invariant borrowing for the title of knights/baronets, before a given name. Fixed Sir supplies the title and /sœʁ/; retained CNRTL independently labels lowercase sir nom masculin and shows lower/uppercase title use. Ordinary English polite address is excluded.

replacements.proposed_text: En France ou au Canada, personne élue à la chambre basse ou unique d’un parlement ; sous la Ve République française, membre de l’Assemblée nationale.
replacements.accepted_text: Personne élue à la chambre basse ou unique d’un parlement : en France, membre de l’Assemblée nationale sous la Ve République ; au Canada, membre de la Chambre des communes ou d’une assemblée législative provinciale ou territoriale.
replacements.reason: Masculine elected representative in France/Canada; accepted meanings explicitly retain French National Assembly and Canadian Commons/provincial/territorial legislatures.

replacements.proposed_text: In France or Canada, an elected member of a parliament’s lower or single chamber; under France’s Fifth Republic, a member of the National Assembly.
replacements.accepted_text: An elected member of a parliament’s lower or single chamber: in France’s Fifth Republic, the National Assembly; in Canada, the House of Commons or a provincial or territorial legislature.
replacements.reason: Masculine elected representative in France/Canada; accepted meanings explicitly retain French National Assembly and Canadian Commons/provincial/territorial legislatures.

replacements.proposed_text: 在法国或加拿大，指议会下院或一院制议会的民选议员；在法国第五共和国，指国民议会议员。

replacements.proposed_text: Au figuré, retrouver des forces, de l’espoir ou de la joie.
replacements.accepted_text: Au figuré et par exagération, retrouver des forces, de l’espoir ou de la joie.
replacements.reason: Figurative and hyperbolic intransitive recovery of strength/hope/joy; causative faire revivre remains intransitive, excluding literal resurrection and transitive reliving.
